480	The Chida, of blessed memory, in his book Pnei David, writes that the angels had a claim
481	against Moshe Rabbenu.
482	Why?
483	They said, this rabbi is not of proper lineage.
484	HaShem said to them, what do you mean, not of proper lineage?
485	This is Moshe Rabbenu, son of Amram: "A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi." How can you say he is not of proper lineage?
486	They said, excuse us, who is his mother?
487	He said to them, what, who is his mother?
488	Yochéved, she was a righteous woman, what do you mean who is his mother?
489	They said, true, but Amram divorced his wife Yochéved.
490	And Yochéved went and married Elitzafan, and bore from him
491	Eldad and Medad.
492	Therefore Eldad and Medad are brothers of Moshe from the same mother but not the same father.
493	These are Eldad and Medad, and so the Ramban writes as well.
494	Afterward Elitzafan and Yochéved decided they were not suited.
495	She divorced him.
496	And returned to Amram.
497	So it turns out that Moshe Rabbenu is a son, when she returned to Amram, she bore Moshe
498	Rabbenu.
499	So Moshe Rabbenu is the son of a man who took back his divorced wife after her remarriage, which is forbidden.
500	Did you understand what happened here?
501	In the Torah it is forbidden to do such a thing.
502	Why is it forbidden?
503	If a man divorced his wife, and she went and married someone else, and now she has divorced
504	him and wants to go back to the first one, her first husband, she cannot do that according to the Torah.
505	Why?
506	So that people won't swap wives.
507	How does that work?
508	Say there are two men here, me and my wife, and another
509	man and his wife.
510	Now, heaven forbid, I set my eye on his wife, and he, heaven forbid, set his eye on my wife.
511	What do we do so that everything is smooth, kosher, Torah-compliant, even in the strictest way?
512	I divorce her, he divorces her.
513	I marry his wife, he marries my wife.
514	We do what we want, then I divorce her, he divorces her.
515	I take back my wife and he takes back his wife.
516	And everything was perfectly by the book, there is no prohibition here.
517	Behold, therefore the Torah was already wise, and said there is no such thing.
518	One who takes back his divorced wife after she remarried can no longer take her back, so that there will be no
519	swapping of spouses.
520	Did you understand this trick?
521	And therefore the angels had a claim about Moshe Rabbenu's lineage.
522	What did the angels say?
523	They said, excuse us, he is the son of one who took back his divorced wife after her remarriage.
524	Yochéved was married to Amram.
525	Amram divorced her, and why did he divorce her?
526	He said, what?
527	"Every son that is born, throw into the Nile," I don't want to bring more children.
528	So he did not bring more children.
529	And then he divorced her.
530	She went, did not want to be alone, and married Elitzafan.
531	She bore Eldad and Medad, Elitzafan divorced her, and she went back to Amram.
532	So now, when Amram took her back, she conceived Moshe.
533	So apparently the angels had a claim against Moshe, that he is the son of one who took back his divorced wife, that the child has a flaw.
534	About this the angels said, "What is one born of woman doing among us?"
535	What does "one born of woman" mean?
536	A woman known to have been taken back after remarriage.
537	What is she doing?
538	HaShem said to them, he comes to receive the Torah.
539	What does it mean, to receive the Torah?
540	Now these laws exist, before this these laws did not exist.
541	So everything is fine with him.
542	Now the real question is, why did HaShem bring Moshe's soul in such a complicated and cumbersome way?
543	Because apparently, setting aside whether they received the Torah or not,
544	the main idea here is that Moshe Rabbenu's soul descended through the generations
545	as though there were a flaw in its descent, of one who takes back his divorced wife after her remarriage.
546	So how can that be?
547	So the Arizal writes, Rabbenu the Arizal writes, that this is a kind
548	of wonderful thing, and he brings it in Shaar HaGilgulim, Introduction 15.
549	He does not speak there about Moshe, but he speaks about the matter of souls of holy people who come into the souls of
550	secular families.
551	You see this to this day.
552	I think this generation, this Shaar HaGilgulim is the most connected to this generation.
553	If you see a secular family that does not keep Torah or mitzvot, and the more they are a husk
554	and the more they hate the Torah and Moshe His servant, and hate and are against, and so on,
555	and one of them returned to teshuvah, and it is known that he does not belong to this family at all.
556	What does it mean, does not belong?
557	He does not belong to them.
558	True, they brought him into the world physically, true, bodily he belongs to them.
559	Physiologically, those are their genes.
560	But in the end, in terms of the soul, he belongs to especially high souls, whom HaShem did not want to bring through
561	families of distinguished Haredim.
562	Because if He brought them through families of distinguished Haredim, the Sitra Achra would accuse them.
563	And they would not succeed in their studies, would not succeed in holiness, would not succeed at anything, they would fall.
564	Because of...
565	because of their holiness.
566	So all day long the Sitra Achra, what does the Gemara say?
567	Page 52 of Tractate Sukkah: the evil inclination leaves the whole world and goes to Israel.
568	It leaves all of Israel, goes to the Torah scholars.
569	It leaves the Torah scholars, goes to the rabbis.
570	The holier you are, the more the evil inclination comes to make you fall.
571	So what does HaShem do so that the Sitra Achra will not provoke those souls?
572	He brings them through the husk.
573	And therefore this person has to deal with a bad family, a bad mother, a wicked father, with people
574	who do not keep Torah, with people who desecrate the festivals.
575	And the Arizal writes, open it up, it's beautiful, it's also not hard to understand, Shaar HaGilgulim, Introduction 15.
576	And he writes there that if we see with our eyes that he grew up and learned Torah
577	a lot, and became a great tzaddik, it is known that what I said is true.
578	And it is known that it is so, that he is a high soul who does not belong at all to this family.
579	So this is a great thing, so this is the reason why HaShem brought Moshe Rabbenu in such a way.
580	Why did He bring his soul down in such a way?
581	So that in the end there would be no accusation against his soul.
582	Who has a greater soul than Moshe Rabbenu?
583	Is there anyone?
584	He is equal to 600,000 of Israel.
585	So in order to bring his soul by way of the husk, it was necessary to bring Moshe's soul through
586	one who takes back his divorced wife after her remarriage.
587	This is the reason why HaShem brought Moshe Rabbenu's soul this way.
588	I said this, I don't remember if I said it here, that I think Mashiach Tzidkenu will be a baal teshuvah.
589	Once I said it in Moshav…, right when I came to give classes there, seven and a half
590	years ago.
591	So I gave a class there, and I said that Mashiach Tzidkenu will be a baal teshuvah.
592	And it angered all the Haredim there, how dare I, what is this.
593	Mashiach Tzidkenu will be a baal teshuvah, and also all the Haredim turn up their noses at you, as if they look down on you.
594	This is another one of the
595	great disappointments of a baal teshuvah.
596	He enters the world of Torah and thinks everything is beautiful, and at least you'd get feedback
597	from the religious, you see worse within what you see.
598	You understand that you have to create your own kingdom, you have to create a bubble, an
599	environment of your own, for yourself, for your children, and not mix in too much.
